title: SDK & client libraries — prioritization workbench for enterprise requests
creator: Lina Zhou
description: Create a lightweight prioritization workbench and decision flow for incoming enterprise SDK/client library requests. The goal is to standardize how we evaluate language bindings (Go, Rust, .NET), auth patterns (SSO/SAML, token refresh, service-to-service), and streaming ergonomics (client backpressure, resumability, transparent reconnects) against SLAs and engineering cost. Deliverables: a scoring rubric, intake form updates, clear routing rules to ENG/Design, and a backlog of candidate work with recommended phasing for Dedicated/Private customers.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Lina Zhou: Kickoff notes added. Customers: two large enterprise accounts requesting first-class Go and .NET SDKs plus SAML auth for on-prem deployments. Support tickets linked in attachments.

2026-02-18 - Miguel Santos: Draft scoring rubric v0.1 created. Proposed axes: customer size & ARR, security bar (requires SAML/KMS), latency sensitivity, expected monthly token volumes, integration effort (engineering months), and strategic alignment. Posted draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/SDK+Prioritization+Workbench

2026-02-25 - Product Review (Lina, Miguel, Keisha - Eng PM, Arjun - Platform Eng): Decided to treat streaming ergonomics separately from language binding requests. Streaming requests get elevated priority when tied to low-latency SLAs or high message volume (>10M tokens/mo).

2026-03-01 - Keisha Thompson (Eng PM): ENG feasibility study requested for Go binding (ENG-2124) and streaming reconnect API (ENG-2330). Estimated 6 sprints for full-featured Go SDK; recommend staged delivery: core client -> streaming -> integrations (auth, telemetry).
2026-03-05 - Support: Provided three anonymized customer logs demonstrating streaming reconnect failure modes. Added to attachments.

2026-03-09 - Miguel Santos: Updated intake form to include explicit fields for (1) required auth types, (2) expected concurrency/throughput, (3) deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), (4) legal/compliance flags. Live at: https://forms.redwood.ai/sdk-request

2026-03-12 - Lina Zhou: PM triage meeting outcome: prioritize Go SDK core client and SAML auth scaffolding for Private customers as Phase 1 (target release: sdk-2026.04). Streaming ergonomics backlog item scoped for Phase 2 pending ENG's reconnect design (ENG-2330).
decision_log: 2026-02-25: Streaming ergonomics and language bindings separated for prioritization to reduce scope and unblock fast wins.
2026-03-01: Adopt staged SDK delivery: core sync/async client -> streaming API -> enterprise auth integrations.
2026-03-12: Phase 1 selected: Go core client + SAML skeleton for Private; defer full streaming ergonomics until ENG-2330 design is validated.
proposed_next_steps: Finalize scoring rubric and convert to automated triage rules in Zendesk/Form handler (owner: Miguel)
Kickoff ENG-2124 (Go core client) with a 6-week milestone plan; confirm resource allocation with Platform Eng
Create PRD for SAML integration pattern for Private deployments; include KMS/HSM considerations (owner: Lina)
Define success metrics for Phase 1: SDK adoption (first 3 customers integrated), integration time, increase in Private deployment conversions
notes_on_tradeoffs: Prioritizing Go core client accelerates enterprise TTV but risks delaying language parity for Rust/.NET — mitigation: publish stable low-level protocol and official gRPC/HTTP bindings to make community contributions easier.
Implementing full streaming reconnects and backpressure now increases scope and delaying initial SDK releases; staged approach preserves progress while ENG prototypes reconnect design in parallel.
